title: add reproducible-build manifest + hashchain indexer for private-installer releases
author: Sofia Patel
description: Introduce a reproducible-build manifest and a signed hashchain indexer for Private Installer releases. Motivation: customers running Private (VPC and on-prem) need strong, verifiable release provenance that supports deterministic rebuilds, incremental delta fetches, and atomic rollbacks. This PR implements: 1) a reproducible-build manifest format (repro-manifest.json) emitted by our build pipelines that records build inputs, pinned toolchain versions, build environment nonce, and a canonical content-addressed artifact list; 2) a hashchain indexer that consumes build manifests and produces a signed, append-only index (index-hashchain.jsonl) where each entry contains the prior entry hash to enable tamper-evident release timelines; 3) dual-signing support in the release pipeline (cosign + GPG) for both individual artifacts (helm charts, installer tarballs, terraform modules) and the produced index; 4) a small installer-side verifier library (bash + Go shim) that validates hashchain continuity and signature coverage before applying upgrades or rollbacks; 5) CI/build changes to emit deterministic archive ordering and stamp SBOM entries so 'repro-manifest.json' can be validated by third parties. The description below documents integration points, rollback story, and operator commands for verification.

files_snippets:
ci/release/workflows/repro-release.yml:  # new workflow step
  - name: Emit reproducible manifest
    run: ./ci/release/indexer/emit-manifest --out repro-manifest.json

installer/verifier/verifier.sh:  # verify chain continuity and signatures
  previous_hash=$(jq -r .prev index-entry.json)
  compute_hash ./artifact.tgz > computed && test \"$previous_hash\" = \$(cat computed)

Sofia Patel (author): Added unit test and fixed a race in the indexer write path; PTAL.
Jordan Kim: Approving after the unit test. One question: how do we handle key rotation for customers that opt to bring their own keys?
Sofia Patel: We added a documented key-rotation hook and a compatibility mode where CI emits both old and new signatures for one release window. See docs/private-installer/release-verification.md
Priya Desai: CI flake observed on acceptance-gke-helm; reran and all checks passed.
ci_log_summary: initial pipeline run: one flaky acceptance test (acceptance-gke-helm) failed, rerun succeeded. All signing checks passed, cosign + gpg artifacts uploaded to release bucket.
release_notes: Add reproducible-build manifests and a tamper-evident hashchain indexer for Private Installer releases. Releases now include dual signatures (cosign + GPG) and a small verifier shipped with the installer to validate release continuity and signatures. Backwards compatible: existing installers will ignore the index if not present.
operator_commands: Verify a release index: curl -sS https://releases.redwood.ai/private/index-hashchain.jsonl | jq -r 'last' > entry.json && ./installer/verifier/verifier.sh entry.json
notes_for_release_team: Ensure CI vault key for cosign is available in release pipeline before rolling this out to release/* branches.
Coordinate with security to publish the GPG verification keyset to the customer trust bundle.
Plan a 2-week crossover window where both old and new index formats are accepted by the installer.
